decisions.statement: The edits beside a subagent's page are the edits that subagent never landed.
An apply drops the rows it landed, so what is left was never landed.
The refusals beside a subagent's page are what the last landing it tried gave.
A run refusing nothing takes that file away, so a file there was never answered.
Every line is appended to the seat rather than replacing what the seat has.
An edit appended says which subagent left it and when the seat took it.
The time a line says is when the seat took the line rather than when the edit was drafted.
When an edit was drafted is said by nothing this move reads.
Every edit one move appends says the same time.
A line that reads as no object is appended unchanged.
A refusal appended is opened by the slug of the subagent whose refusal it was.
One blank line parts the refusals of two subagents.
The readings beside a subagent's page are what that subagent has read.
A reading appended says the agent id that reading was made by.
The agent id is read off the page that is going.
A page stating no agent id moves no reading.
A reading appended is beside the seat rather than among the seat's own readings.
A reading the seat keeps goes back to the page the agent id it says takes up.
A reading goes back without the agent id the seat kept it under.
A reading the seat keeps under another agent id is left where it is.
A reading goes back before what the page already holds rather than after it.
The seat's file goes once the last reading it kept has gone back.
A reading the seat keeps is dropped where its agent id is handed in as gone.
A reading naming no agent id is never dropped that way.
Which agents are gone is handed in rather than judged here.
Nothing here weighs whether an agent handed in as gone could return.
Which agents a seat keeps readings for is answered off the seat's own file.
A reading goes where its agent's last record predates the client handed in.
That agent's last record is read where the module for outliving reads it.
The client's start and the transcript are handed in rather than reached for.
A reading kept under a seat id other than the one handed in is left alone.
No reading goes for how long its agent has been quiet.
The seat's file goes once the last reading it kept has been dropped.
A subagent with nothing beside it moves nothing.
What was moved is taken from beside the subagent rather than copied.
A second move over the same subagent therefore moves nothing.
A sweep refused after a move leaves what moved reachable from the seat.
A write here takes a lock keyed on the file the write writes.
The paths written are the ones the seat page type names rather than spelled here.
A page taken away that is no subagent moves nothing.
The seat a subagent's edits move onto is the seat that subagent's page names.
A subagent whose seat the index files no page for moves nothing.
Nothing here takes a page away.
Nothing here judges whether a subagent is gone.

definition: what a subagent left beside its page, moved between that page and the seat that dispatched it
